policy.bsfcStatus: engineering fuel-consumption scenario, not an historical engine map
policy.load: Standard fixed air-to-air guns, full ammunition, pilot, oil and service equipment; no bombs, rockets, external tanks or optional gun pods. Removable racks excluded; standard fixed fittings retained.
policy.powerExtension: Optional pressure-lapse engineering continuation above the last source node, through 40000 ft. Never presented as measured or source-supported power.
policy.normal: Recommended routine climb rating. The same engine rating is used for all Normal metrics; its documented time limit remains active.
policy.combat: Highest admitted combat rating and its documented allowance; return to the approved Normal rating when exhausted. Overlapping limits use a common high-power clock, not additive timer resets.
policy.climb: Normal follows the manual speed schedule. Combat compares legal contiguous boost-use windows and retains the quickest modeled window, then replays it with changing fuel mass. Selected-altitude tests start independently with fresh allowance; full climbs never reset it.
policy.qualification: Operational benchmark scenarios, not historical turn validation. Source/variant transfers, load reconstructions and rating conversions remain explicitly qualified. The historical replay panels stay unchanged.
policy.injection: Separate per-aircraft toggle at Combat power, disabled where not fitted. Dry Combat is always available independently of injection; a charged reservoir is carried in either state. Injection uses the same high-power clock as dry Combat, not a new additive allowance.

spit.title: A&AEE BS.543 Merlin 66 report, sections 2.4/3 and Table II
spit.facts: 2850 rpm/+12 climb for 60 min; 3000 rpm/+18 combat for 5 min. Original long combat climbs had a special test concession. 7485-lb takeoff mass.

spit-notes.title: AP 1565J P & L PN, September 1946, paras 40/51/54
spit-notes.facts: Normal +12/2850; combat +18/3000 for Merlin 66. Recommended routine climb 180 mph IAS. Normal supercharger change differs from combat. Later manual is procedural corroboration, not a BS.543 flight measurement.

p51.title: AAF Manual 51-127-5, 15 August 1945, printed pp.52/55
p51.facts: Normal 46inHg/2700 rpm after takeoff; military 61/3000; WEP 67/3000. D/K procedure with V-1650-3/-7, transferred explicitly to B-15 engine, not its airframe mass.

p51-trial.title: Wright Field Eng-47-1749-A, 20 May 1944, 43-24777
p51-trial.facts: 9335 lb with 265 US gal; 125 lb heavier than combat load with 1260 rounds and rear tank empty. 67inHg present WEP, 75 proposed with 44-1 fuel. Rack-free speed observations separate from racked climb.

p47.title: P-47B original torquemeter trials and preliminary handbook
p47.facts: R-2800-21 normal 1625 bhp/2550 rpm; military 2000/2700, five-minute policy in 41-5902 report. No later-variant ADI rating admitted. 41-5942 is eight-gun donor; 41-5902 had six guns.

p47-notes.title: AAF Manual 50-5, printed pp.44-45
p47-notes.facts: Normal and military climbs separately prescribed; use later manual for policy corroboration only, not a D-model injection transfer to the B.

p38.title: TO 01-75F-1, P-38D-G, revised 30 September 1944
p38.facts: Normal maximum 2600 rpm; military 3000 rpm time-limited. OCR renders the minute figure ambiguously: a conservative five-minute engineering allowance is selected pending original-page verification. Later J/L 54inHg is excluded.

p38-trial.title: FS-M-19-1538-A, 42-12687, 10 February 1943
p38-trial.facts: 13900 lb with 180 US gal, two .50 guns/400 rounds and 20mm/50 rounds; 44.7inHg/3000 rpm climb. Turbo/carburetor restrictions preserved. Standard four-gun/full-ammo load requires reconstruction.

fw.title: D(Luft)T 2190 A-2/A-3/A-4, October 1942 status, July 1943 edition
fw.facts: BMW 801 D2: climb/combat 2400 rpm/1.32 ata, 30 min; emergency 2700/1.42, 3 min. Generic rating transfer to 783 remains an engineering scenario, not proof that its earlier test used emergency power.

fw-trial.title: Flugbericht Fw190/783 Nr.1
fw-trial.facts: 3870 kg takeoff, BMW801D2, combat power and long intake; source flight power and inlet model retained.

bf.title: Bf109 F1-F4 handbook May 1941, DB601E installation; source register v4.1
bf.facts: DB601E F4 installation confirmed. Numerical 1.30/2500 and 1.42/2700 curves and duration limits remain the existing qualified secondary inputs; this handbook OCR did not independently verify the rating cells. No GM1 or later DB605 rating admitted.

f4u.title: US Navy F4U-4 Standard Aircraft Characteristics, March 1946, pp.5-6
f4u.facts: R-2800-18W normal 1700/2600; military 2100/2800; combat with water injection 2450/2800. WEP-altitude shape is an engineering manifold/critical-height transfer, not newly digitized original engine curves.

f4u-maker.title: Vought F4U-4 specification
f4u-maker.facts: Six .50 guns; R2800-18W water-injected 2450 hp; 534 US gal includes two 150-gal external tanks, leaving 234 internal.

f4u-duration.title: F4U-4 type history: five-minute 2450hp water rating
f4u-duration.facts: Corroborates the five-minute water/methanol rating; does not establish installed fluid mass, flow, cooling or altitude-specific power.

spitfire_lfix_bs543.loadQualification: Full-ammo service fit assumed in source gross mass; 85 Imperial gal converted to US gallons. Not an independently weighed standard combat specimen.
spitfire_lfix_bs543.speedQualification: Later manual routine IAS schedule; existing BF274 position-error correction used only within its source speed range.
spitfire_lfix_bs543.ratingEvidence: Rating limits corroborated by the matched trial and pilot notes; Normal BHP uses a pressure/RPM proxy.

bf109f4.armament: 1 x MG151/20 (200 rounds), 2 x MG17 (500 rounds/gun)
bf109f4.loadQualification: Existing 2890-kg full-service reference with assumed full 400-L fuel. Full ammunition and equipment are a declared service-load reconstruction.

combat.label: Emergency 1.42 ata / 2700 rpm
combat.qualification: Existing secondary rating curve and one-minute limit; original clearance cells unresolved.

bf109f4.speedQualification: 250-260km/h low-altitude climb, decreasing aloft: engineering schedule pending exact F4 manual extraction. IAS=CAS scenario, explicitly uncalibrated.
bf109f4.ratingEvidence: Provisional rating/clearance scenario: existing secondary DB601E inputs; original limit cells not independently verified.

p47b.loadQualification: Eight-gun 41-5942 gross mass transferred to same-engine 41-5902 aerodynamic reference; full 305-gal fuel/full-ammo attribution is an explicit loading assumption, not a recovered weighing sheet.
p47b.speedQualification: AAF manual 155-160mph low-altitude range; altitude reduction is an engineering schedule, not a new exact B-model manual transcription.
p47b.ratingEvidence: Source dry ratings and verified 2:1 gearing; no later water-injected engine transferred.

p51b.loadQualification: Source combat mass 9335-125=9210 lb with rear tank empty and 180 US gal. 50% of total 265-gal capacity fits wing tanks; rear tank remains empty for maneuvering. Original clean calibration is used, not subtraction of the local rack fit at every speed.
p51b.speedQualification: Normal manual family schedule, with engineering continuation above 25000 ft. V1650-7 transfer explicit; proposed 75inHg excluded.
p51b.ratingEvidence: Manual-family 46/2700 and 67/3000 transfer to the modeled V1650-7; experimental 75inHg excluded.

fw190a4.armament: 2 x MG151/20, 2 x MGFF/M, 2 x MG17; full standard ammunition
fw190a4.loadQualification: 3870-kg source gross and assumed full 524-L internal fuel/full-ammo service fit; exact trial ammunition not recovered.

combat.label: Emergency 1.42 ata / 2700 rpm
combat.qualification: 1730/1520 PS manual rating ratio, same BMW801D2, transferred to trial intake model.

fw190a4.speedQualification: 270km/h low-altitude climb scenario, decreasing aloft; exact manual speed graph remains untranscribed.
fw190a4.ratingEvidence: BMW801D2 manual rating transfer to the trial aircraft; emergency altitude shape is an engineering conversion.

p38g.loadQualification: Source underarmed test converted by engineering +595 lb: two guns 122 lb, 1600 extra .50 rounds at .26 lb, 100 extra 20mm rounds at .57 lb. Source 400-round interpretation and ammunition masses are assumptions; 306-gal capacity needs exact weighing-chart corroboration. No false full-service test identity.

normal.label: Normal 37inHg / 2600 rpm
normal.qualification: 37inHg normal limit from qualified early-model manual OCR; original engine chart still needs confirmation. Lower-rating BHP uses the declared pressure/RPM proxy.

combat.label: Military 44.7inHg / 3000 rpm
combat.qualification: Report power curve; conservative five-minute allowance pending original manual restriction cell. 48inHg single-point trial and later 54inHg excluded.

p38g.speedQualification: Family normal-climb schedule; exact G-model correction not established. IAS=CAS scenario.
p38g.ratingEvidence: Qualified early-model manual OCR: normal MAP and military duration still require original-cell verification; later J/L boost excluded.

f4u4.loadQualification: 12500-lb clean normal-fighter trial; full 234-gal/internal ammunition attribution is a reconstruction. Standard fixed fittings remain in the source polar; no detachable bomb racks, bombs or rockets added.
f4u4.speedQualification: Normal-fighter climb-speed engineering schedule pending AN01-45HB-1 chart extraction.

injection.label: WEP water / 2800 rpm
injection.qualification: 2450/2100 source sea-level ratio. Above sea level, manifold/critical-height transfer is an engineering model; 5-min allowance/20lb per min are explicit conservative scenarios pending exact handbook water schedule.

f4u4.ratingEvidence: Source sea-level dry/water ratings; injection altitude shape, fluid mass and flow remain engineering scenarios.
